figures.cap: directed road network with minimum cut

parts.latex:
The diagram below shows a network of directed roads on which vehicles travel from a shopping centre at S to a car park at P. The maximum capacity (vehicles per hour) is shown, and the minimum cut is shown as the dashed line.

\exfigure{2846_q7b_1}
How many possible paths are there through the network of roads from S to P?
Explain why the capacity of the minimum cut is 800 vehicles per hour.

solutions.latex:
The minimum cut passes through edges $AC$, $DC$ and $FP$, so its capacity is the sum of their capacities.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Min cut} &= 200 + 300 + 300 \\ &= 800 \text{ vehicles per hour} \end{aligned}$$

2846_q7b_1.notes: Directed road network S→P with capacities and the minimum cut as a fine dashed curve following the crop's path. Filled Latex heads are kept where the crop puts its arrowheads along each edge. Vertex letters are maths italic. The leftover colour is the scan's stroke weight, dash length and font glyphs. Rules 1, 3, 4, 19.

figures.cap: flow network with source, sink and a dashed cut
solution sketch: flow network with cut edges 9, 6 and 4 circled

solutions.latex:
The capacity of a cut is the sum of the capacities crossing it in the forward direction.

$$9+6+4=19$$

The $4$ flowing back across the cut is not counted.

\exfigure{3300_qD8_s1}

Hence the answer is A.

3300_qD8_1.notes: Flow network: 7 nodes at the crop's pixel positions, edges 0.6pt with filled Latex arrowheads at mid-edge (the 4 runs from the lower-right node back to the middle node, as in the crop). Capacities, source and sink labelled; dashed cut redrawn as a smooth house-aux curve along the crop's path. In round 2 I moved the cut and the upper 4 and 6 labels onto the crop's positions. Rules 1, 3, 4, 6a, 19.

3300_qD8_s1.notes: Same network and cut as 3300_qD8_1. The solution's circles round the counted cut capacities 9, 6 and 4 are kept as black circles. The orange and green crossing arrows were dropped as teacher marks (rules 6, 17); the circles alone show that the backward 4 is not counted. The remaining red is those dropped scribbles and the slightly different hand-drawn circle shapes.
